title: INKA
bottom_line: The state owns INKA through Danantara: Danantara Asset Management holds 99% and the Republic a 1% golden share (INKA's own disclosure, backed by a December 2025 regulation), and KAI, its main customer, began taking INKA over in September 2026, with the merger due to take effect on 1 January 2027 (confirmed by press). The group is small and mostly described by the companies themselves: INKA Multi Solusi (99.86%) makes components, interiors and export wagons and owns trading, maintenance and consulting arms; Rekaindo (49%, with Japan's Nippon Sharyo and Sumitomo) makes electrical, door and propulsion parts; and a 2020 joint venture with Stadler for the Banyuwangi plant is no longer listed. Named suppliers are mostly other state firms under 2018 supply agreements (Barata castings and couplers, Krakatau Steel, Pindad, INTI, Inalum; company claims), plus Ceper foundries for brake blocks and DTECH for seats (confirmed by press), while the new commuter trains' traction gear comes from Japan's Toyo Denki (supplier's claim). Buyers are KAI and KAI Commuter at home and Bangladesh, the Philippines and, through Australia's UGL, New Zealand's KiwiRail; commuter-train deliveries are a year late, and INKA reported a Rp677bn loss and Rp4.7T of loans in September 2026 (confirmed).

entities.name: PT INKA (Persero)
entities.what: State rolling-stock maker founded 18 May 1981: locomotives, passenger cars, KRL electric trains, LRT and freight wagons; 22.5-ha Madiun works plus a Banyuwangi (Kalipuro) plant opened in 2023; local content up from 33% to 52% (May 2026); a Rp677bn loss and Rp4.7T of loans flagged in Sep 2026.

entities.name: Republic of Indonesia
entities.what: Holds INKA's 1% Seri A Dwiwarna (golden) share and 1% of Danantara Asset Management; puts new capital into INKA through Danantara (PMN).

entities.name: BPI Danantara
entities.legal_name: Badan Pengelola Investasi Daya Anagata Nusantara
entities.what: State investment agency set up in 2025; owns 99% of Danantara Asset Management, receives state capital meant for INKA (PP 52/2025) and on 18 May 2026 mandated KAI and INKA to study a merger.

entities.name: Danantara Asset Management (DAM)
entities.what: Danantara's operating holding for state firms (governance, restructuring); holds INKA's Seri B shares (99%); owned 99% by BPI Danantara and 1% by the Republic (Jun 2025).

entities.name: BP BUMN
entities.legal_name: Badan Pengaturan Badan Usaha Milik Negara
entities.what: State-enterprise regulator; INKA lists it with BPI Danantara as its supervising body since 2025 (after the Ministry of SOEs); its head ordered INKA to draft a grand transformation plan (Sep 2026).

entities.name: PT INKA Multi Solusi (IMS)
entities.what: INKA's 99.86% subsidiary, founded 2009 as PT Railindo Global Karya and renamed 2015: components, interior panels, fibreglass, export freight wagons, train air-conditioners, Pertashop kiosks; 11-ha plant at Desa Bagi, Kab. Madiun; parent of IMSS, IMST and IMSC.

entities.name: PT IMST
entities.what: IMS's 95% trading arm (2015) for railway components at home and abroad; exported 30 car-sets of passenger bogie frames to Bangladesh (Nov 2022) and placed the 2022 seat pilot order with DTECH.

entities.name: PT IMSS
entities.what: IMS's 95% maintenance arm (2014): train, spare-part and plant-machine maintenance; KAI Commuter KRL maintenance in Yogyakarta (2024-25) and the 80-month LRT Jabodebek maintenance work (Oct 2024).

entities.name: PT IMSC
entities.what: IMS's 90% consulting arm (2017): design, engineering and management consulting for rail and transport; named by DTECH's academy as a partner on the INKA seat project.

entities.name: PT Rekaindo Global Jasa (REKA)
entities.what: Engineering and component firm founded 25 Nov 1998 (INKA 49%, Nippon Sharyo 39%, Sumitomo 10%, INKA staff cooperative Kopinka 2%): electrical panels, propulsion boxes (SIV, VVVF box), sliding plug doors, sleeper-seat electrics, passenger displays; most output goes into INKA trains.

entities.name: PT Stadler INKA Indonesia
entities.what: Foreign-investment joint venture of INKA and Stadler Rail; articles signed in Jakarta on 30 Jul 2020 to run the Banyuwangi powered-train plant once orders came; stake split never published; absent from INKA's 2026 subsidiary list.

entities.name: Keluarga Besar INKA (staff association)
entities.legal_name: Yayasan Keluarga Besar INKA / Perkumpulan Keluarga Besar INKA (PKBI)
entities.what: INKA staff family body that holds 0.14% of IMS and the 10% of IMSC that IMS does not; INKA's pages call it both a yayasan (foundation) and a perkumpulan (association).

entities.name: Stadler Rail AG
entities.what: Swiss train builder; signed a joint-venture agreement with INKA on 20 Sep 2019 for aluminium rolling stock at Banyuwangi; technology transfer was tied to an order for 500 suburban cars (plus a 500-car option).

entities.name: Nippon Sharyo
entities.what: Japanese rolling-stock maker; holds 39% of REKA and visited it as a main shareholder in Apr 2024.

entities.name: Sumitomo Corporation
entities.what: Japanese trading house; holds 10% of REKA and visited it with Nippon Sharyo in Apr 2024.

entities.name: PT KAI
entities.what: National railway operator and INKA's main customer (612 new-generation cars 2023-26, 31 LRT Jabodebek trainsets); taking over INKA by a conditional share transfer that began Sep 2026, effective 1 Jan 2027, with INKA as its manufacturing subholding.

entities.name: KAI Commuter (KCI)
entities.what: Jabodetabek commuter-train operator; ordered 16 new KRL trainsets (iE305 / CLI-225, Mar 2023) and a 19-trainset retrofit (Nov 2023) from INKA; 7 of the 16 had arrived by Sep 2026.

entities.name: Bangladesh Railway
entities.what: State railway and INKA's biggest export buyer of passenger coaches: 150 delivered in 2016, 50 broad-gauge ordered Jun 2017, then 200 metre-gauge; Banalata Express launched Apr 2019.

entities.name: Philippine National Railways (PNR)
entities.what: Philippine state railway; bought 6 INKA diesel multiple units and 3 diesel-hydraulic locomotive trainsets in 2018 (about US$57M in all); locomotives and 15 coaches arrived Dec 2020.

entities.name: UGL Rail Services
entities.what: Australian rail contractor and INKA export client since 2021: 262 + 450 container flat wagons for KiwiRail (2021-24), 450 more ordered Jul 2024, 340 SOW6 wagons (2026) and 50 C44 locomotive platforms through 2028.

entities.name: KiwiRail
entities.what: New Zealand state rail and ferry operator; end user of the INKA-built container flat wagons bought through UGL (Wagon Replacement Programme).

entities.name: DTECH-ENGINEERING
entities.what: Salatiga CNC machine and parts maker; makes INKA's executive and luxury train seats (Rp2.5B pilot 2022; 1,400 executive + 100 luxury seats ordered 2023) with Madiun vocational schools.

entities.name: PT Barata Indonesia
entities.what: State foundry and engineering firm: bogie castings (side frames, bolsters), couplers and axle boxes for KAI and INKA; signed INKA's component supply agreement in Jan 2018.

entities.name: PT Krakatau Steel
entities.what: State steelmaker; signed INKA's material and component supply agreement on 18 Jan 2018, the day of the LRT Jabodebek contract.

entities.name: PT Pindad
entities.what: State defence manufacturer; signed INKA's Jan 2018 supply agreement; a Transport Ministry document says it worked with INKA on LRT Jabodebek traction motors (snippet).

entities.name: PT INTI
entities.what: State electronics and telecom maker; signed INKA's Jan 2018 material and component supply agreement (products not stated).

entities.name: PT Inalum
entities.what: State aluminium producer; named in Jan 2018 as aluminium-plate supplier for INKA's LRT car bodies; in Nov 2018 INKA said Inalum had been asked to make it.

entities.name: Koperasi Batur Jaya (Ceper foundries)
entities.what: Cooperative of 168 Ceper foundry firms (2019); makes metallic train brake blocks under order contracts from KAI and INKA (200,000-220,000 a year in 2016); composite blocks in testing (2019).

entities.name: Toyo Denki Seizo
entities.what: Japanese traction-equipment maker; supplies the VVVF traction system (RG6061-A-M) and pantograph for INKA's KRL iE305 (CLI-225); discussed technology transfer with REKA in 2024.

entities.name: IRMA (rail component makers' association)
entities.legal_name: Asosiasi Industri Manufaktur dan Penunjang Perkeretaapian Indonesia
entities.what: Association of about 50 rail-component firms (metal, rubber, plastic, research, consultants) set up with the Industry Ministry in 2016; INKA is a member.

entities.name: Indonesia Eximbank (LPEI)
entities.what: State export-credit agency; financed INKA's Bangladesh coaches (Rp270bn, 2016), IMS's New Zealand wagons (US$11.9M, 2024) and INKA's SOW6 wagons (US$8.5M, 2026).

entities.name: Politeknik Negeri Madiun (PNM)
entities.what: State polytechnic with a rail programme; INKA vocational partner since 2019, part of the 2022 DTECH seat agreement, buyer of an INKA hybrid test train (2023) and a REKA partner (2023, 2026).

entities.name: Universitas Maarif Hasyim Latif (UMAHA)
entities.what: Private university that launched the 'CNC Nusantara' laser-cutting machine on 14 Aug 2025 and signed an MoU with REKA to explore its use for rail-industry work.

entities.name: Bambang Jatmika
entities.what: President Director of INKA on its organisation page (Oct 2026); earlier INKA's Director of Quality Management (snippet); appointment date not found.

entities.name: Eko Purwanto
entities.what: INKA President Director from early 2023 (signed the KAI and KCI contracts on 9 Mar 2023) to at least Oct 2025.

entities.name: Budi Noviantoro
entities.what: INKA President Director from 15 Jan 2018 until at least May 2022; signed the PNR contracts (2018), the Stadler joint-venture agreement (Sep 2019) and the KAI Commuter KRL MoU (May 2022).

entities.name: Puguh Dwi Tjahjono
entities.what: President Director of IMS (listed as acting by INKA); INKA's GM Corporate Secretary in 2020, when he announced the Stadler joint venture.

entities.name: Bambang Sutrisno
entities.what: INKA's GM Corporate Secretary (acting in Oct 2025, GM by Sep 2026) and President Commissioner of IMS on IMS's own site (2026).

entities.name: Edwyn Dwi Cahyo
entities.what: Director of Finance, HR and Risk at IMS (acting per INKA, 2026); INKA's acting GM Corporate Secretariat in Oct 2024.

entities.name: A. Wishnudartha Pagehgiri
entities.what: IMS commissioner (INKA page, 2026); led IMSC at its launch after managing INKA's airport-train project (also spelled Wisnudharta).

entities.name: Adib Ardhian
entities.what: President Director of REKA (INKA's 2023 listing; signed the UMAHA CNC MoU on 14 Aug 2025, spelled Adib Ardian there).

entities.name: Wai Wahdan
entities.what: President Director of IMST in 2022; at the DTECH seat signing (May 2022) and the Bangladesh bogie-frame export (Nov 2022).

entities.name: Peter Spuhler
entities.what: Chairman of Stadler Rail's board; signed the INKA joint-venture agreement on 20 Sep 2019.

entities.name: Dony Oskaria
entities.what: Head of BP BUMN and COO of Danantara (Sep-Oct 2026); President Director of Danantara Asset Management in Jun 2025; said in Sep 2026 that INKA was 'not in good condition'.

entities.name: Bobby Rasyidin
entities.what: President Director of KAI; said KAI will be the holding and INKA a subholding (Jun 2026) and reported the KRL delays and recall (Sep 2026).

links.detail: Holds INKA's Seri B shares, 99% (INKA's own disclosure, latest deed 2 Feb 2026).
Holds the 1% Seri A Dwiwarna share; PP 52/2025 keeps that 1% while adding new state capital.

PP 52/2025 (30 Dec 2025): Rp473bn of 2025 state capital to BPI Danantara, passed on as new INKA shares for KRL capacity, propulsion development and a bogie plant; INKA says paid-up capital became Rp2.69T (deed 5 Jan 2026).
BPI Danantara owns 99% of DAM; the Republic owns 1%.

Regulator and supervisor, not a shareholder: its head Dony Oskaria told INKA to draft a grand transformation plan (Sep 2026); INKA lists BP BUMN and BPI Danantara as its supervising bodies since 2025.
Mandated KAI and INKA on 18 May 2026 to run due diligence and a full study on combining them; KAI calls the merger a Danantara directive.
Planned takeover: a conditional share transfer (inbreng) of INKA into KAI began Sep 2026; consolidation effective 1 Jan 2027; KAI to be the holding, INKA a manufacturing subholding. Stake not stated.
INKA 99.86%, Keluarga Besar INKA 0.14%. Founded 23 Dec 2009 as PT Railindo Global Karya; INKA took over 90% on 28 Nov 2014 and renamed it IMS in 2015.
Holds 0.14% of IMS (named 'Yayasan Keluarga Besar INKA' on INKA's page).
95% stake; IMSS set up in 2014 for railway maintenance and services.
95% stake; IMST set up in 2015 to trade railway components locally and overseas.
90% stake; IMSC set up in 2017 for rail and transport consulting, design and engineering.
Took the 10% of IMSC not held by IMS ('Perkumpulan Keluarga Besar INKA', PKBI).
49% stake (Nippon Sharyo 39%, Sumitomo 10%, INKA staff cooperative Kopinka 2%); INKA lists REKA as its subsidiary.
39% stake; visited REKA as a main shareholder on 25-26 Apr 2024.
10% stake; visited REKA with Nippon Sharyo on 25-26 Apr 2024.
Co-founder: articles of association signed 30 Jul 2020 to run the Banyuwangi powered-train plant 'depending on orders'; stake not stated; not on INKA's 2026 subsidiary list.
Co-founder under the JV agreement signed 20 Sep 2019 (Bussnang per railway-news, Zurich per INKA); technology transfer only after an order for 500 suburban cars.
Signed a letter of intent on 20 Sep 2019 to join the joint venture as a shareholder; no record that it did.
Main customer: contracts signed 9 Mar 2023 for 612 stainless-steel new-generation cars (2023-26 replacement programme) and 10 luxury cars for Argo Lawu, Argo Dwipangga and Taksaka.
Built the 31 LRT Jabodebek trainsets (186 cars) ordered by KAI under the 18 Jan 2018 contract; line opened 28 Aug 2023.
INKA brought IMSS in for the 80-month maintenance service agreement on the 31 LRT Jabodebek trainsets.
Investigated and repaired the corrugated gangway bellows on LRT Jabodebek trains.

16 new KRL trainsets (iE305 / CLI-225; MoU 9 May 2022, contract 9 Mar 2023) plus a 19-trainset retrofit (3 Nov 2023); by Sep 2026 only 7 of 16 delivered and 7 recalled for a component fix; output 2-3 sets a year against 8 planned.
Maintenance contract for KRL-KFW trains, Area 6 Yogyakarta, 2024-2025, signed 1 Mar 2024.
150 coaches delivered Nov 2016 (100 metre-gauge, 50 broad-gauge), 50 broad-gauge coaches contracted 20 Jun 2017, Banalata Express launched 25 Apr 2019.
Exported 30 car-sets of passenger-coach bogie frames to Chittagong on 11 Nov 2022 using state-firm vendors; buyer not named, Bangladesh Railway is assumed.
4 DMU trainsets (US$21.4M) and 3 diesel-hydraulic locomotive trainsets (US$26M) contracted 28 May 2018, after 2 DMUs (US$9.7M) on 22 Jan 2018.
Fourth UGL contract since 2021, signed 30 Jul 2024: 450 more container flat-top wagons for KiwiRail, about Rp291bn, due 2025.
50 locomotive platforms (underframes for UGL's C44 ESACi diesel-electric locos); first 2 shipped 14 Feb 2025, the rest through 2028.
340 SOW6 freight wagons for KiwiRail's network (200 shipped by Jul 2026), financed by Indonesia Eximbank.
IMS delivered the earlier UGL orders: 712 container flat-top wagons (262 by Aug 2023, then 450 through Dec 2024); IMS signed the first 262-wagon contract in 2021 (IMS milestones).
UGL hands the INKA-built wagons to KiwiRail as end user; the INKA-UGL-KiwiRail project was a finalist for the 2025 ARA Rail Freight Excellence Award.
Delivered a hybrid diesel-electric test train with pantograph and hydrogen fuel cell to the polytechnic in 2023.
Executive and luxury train seats: Rp2.5B pilot in 2022, then 1,400 executive and 100 luxury seats ordered in 2023.
IMST issued the order confirmation for the train-seat pilot at the 11 May 2022 signing in Madiun.
DTECH's academy lists IMSC with INKA as partners on the seat project.

Supplies INKA the same spare parts it sells KAI (couplers, axle boxes) and bogie components; made the bogies under INKA's Malaysia wagons (Aug 2016); also signed INKA's supply agreement on 18 Jan 2018 (INKA).
Signed INKA's material and component supply agreement on 18 Jan 2018.
Signed INKA's supply agreement on 18 Jan 2018; a Transport Ministry document says Pindad worked on LRT Jabodebek traction-motor parts (shaft, short-circuit ring, housing) (snippet).
Signed INKA's material and component supply agreement on 18 Jan 2018; products not stated.
Named in Jan 2018 as aluminium-plate supplier for the LRT car bodies; in Nov 2018 INKA's CEO said Inalum had been asked to make it, so delivery is unconfirmed.
Brake blocks under order contracts from KAI and INKA (Industry Minister, Aug 2016); 200,000-220,000 blocks a year.
Metallic brake blocks for KAI for 27 years by 2019; composite blocks in testing with the ministry's B4T lab.

VVVF-IGBT traction system (RG6061-A-M) and pantograph for INKA's KRL iE305 (CLI-225), per Toyo Denki's 30 Nov 2023 order notice cited on Wikipedia; INKA's CEO said propulsion, brakes, wheelsets and software were imported (Mar 2023).
Visits in Apr and Dec 2024 on technology transfer and commercial and technical service for certain components.
Electrical panels, propulsion boxes, doors and sleeper-seat electrics (REKA site: 'most output supports INKA'); component-development agreement signed 15 Jul 2025.

11-ha Desa Bagi plant supplies INKA with components, interior panels and fibreglass; IMS also manages INKA's Madiun workshop (since 2020) and supplied LRT Jabodebek interior panels in 2019 (IMS milestones).
Member of IRMA (about 50 component firms); the Industry Ministry said in Mar 2018 that local suppliers met about 70% of component needs and urged INKA to open up to small firms.
US$8.5M export working-capital credit for 340 SOW6 wagons to New Zealand (Aug 2026); earlier Rp270bn for Bangladesh coaches (Feb 2016, per INKA).
US$11.9M of financing and guarantees for IMS's wagon exports to New Zealand (2024).
Signed the 11 May 2022 'industry arm' agreement for train seats with INKA, DTECH and SMK PGRI 1 Mejayan; rail D4 class with INKA since 2019 (INKA).
In the 2022 seat agreement the polytechnic supplies design staff and operators; DTECH supplies machines and management.
Cooperation agreements on vocational training and rail-industry work (Nov 2023, Aug 2026).
REKA signed a Tridharma MoU at the launch of UMAHA's 'CNC Nusantara' laser-cutting machine, to explore using it for rail-industry needs.
President Director on INKA's organisation page (accessed 16 Oct 2026); appointment date not found.
President Director; signed the KAI and KCI contracts on 9 Mar 2023 and hosted the DPR visit on 3 Oct 2025.
Appointed President Director on 15 Jan 2018 (SK-09/MBU/01/2018); still in office in May 2022; an acting president director was in place by Feb 2023.
President Director of IMS (INKA lists him as acting).
INKA's General Manager Corporate Secretary in Aug 2020.
INKA's General Manager Corporate Secretary; issued INKA's reply on the Rp677bn loss.
President Commissioner (Komisaris Utama) on IMS's organisation page (accessed Oct 2026).
Director of Finance, HR and Risk Management at IMS (acting per INKA).
Acting General Manager of INKA's Corporate Secretariat; spoke for INKA in Oct 2024.
Listed on IMS's board of commissioners.
Led IMSC at its launch (previously INKA's airport-train project manager).
President Director of REKA (2023 listing; signed the UMAHA MoU in Aug 2025).
President Director of IMST in May and Nov 2022.
Chairman of Stadler's board; signed the INKA joint-venture agreement.
Head of BP BUMN.
Chief Operating Officer of Danantara.
President Director of Danantara Asset Management (as of Jun 2025).
President Director of KAI; leads the INKA takeover.
